person: Reggie Banks is a 61-year-old part-time finance person, three days a week, at a small snack brand that also sells direct to consumers through an online store and takes cards through a processor. He has ten open card disputes and the founder wants to know how many are real losses versus ones the brand can prove. He is methodical, reads at 175% zoom with a high-contrast theme, and wants every dispute shown line by line with amounts he can add up. He signs nothing until he has seen the evidence behind it.
stated_up_front: I have ten open card disputes on our web store and I need to know which ones we can win and which we should just accept. Go through them one at a time with the amounts, and don't submit or accept anything until I've seen the lines.

facts.truth: Ten open disputes, totaling $1,486.40 across all of them.
Crunchwell Snacks, direct web store selling cases of granola clusters and seed crackers; typical order $48 to $212.
Reggie prepares everything but the founder, Dana Whitfield, wants him to be the one who signs, so he signs each representment and acceptance himself.
Order 4417 for $96.00 (a 6-case crackers order) never left the warehouse because the item was out of stock; the customer wrote twice asking where it was.
Order 4388 for $58.50: Reggie told the customer by email on September 14 that a refund would be issued, and it was never processed, so she disputed it as 'credit not processed'.
Order 4402 for $212.00 shows delivered September 22 to the full street address with signature 'M. Okafor'; the customer claims non-receipt.
Order 4395 for $74.25 was already refunded on September 19 through the store, and the customer disputed afterward anyway.
One dispute for $189.90 where the cardholder has only one earlier undisputed order, from August.
He wants totals broken into lines he can add himself and a clear split between amounts that are already settled and amounts the brand might recover.
Works in a browser at 175% zoom with a high-contrast theme and loses his place in wide tables, so he wants short lists, not wide grids.

unknowns: What Compelling Evidence 3.0 requires or how many earlier orders it needs
The exact processor response deadline for each dispute versus the network deadline
What the reason codes like 13.1, 13.3, 13.6, 10.4 and 4837 mean
Whether a device match counts if the customer changed browsers
